preheader: DoorDash buys Instacart for $17B, AI disproves CS theory, and Rybakina clinches No. 1.

lead.headline: DoorDash Agrees to Acquire Instacart for $17 Billion
lead.body: DoorDash has agreed to acquire rival delivery service Instacart in a deal valued at $17 billion. The transaction brings together DoorDash's dominant restaurant takeout platform with Instacart's extensive grocery delivery network.
lead.why: Large horizontal acquisitions show how logistics companies try to expand market power and unit economics, giving you a real-world case study for corporate strategy.

stories.headline: Eli Lilly Q3 Revenue Rises 39% to $24.4 Billion
stories.body: Eli Lilly reported a 39% increase in third-quarter revenue to $24.4 billion, driven by strong sales of Mounjaro and Zepbound. The pharmaceutical company raised its full-year guidance following the results.
stories.why: Tracking how pharmaceutical companies scale high-demand products highlights core valuation and revenue forecasting methods used in financial analysis.

stories.headline: Bain Capital in Talks for $500 Million India Real Estate Deal
stories.body: Indian real estate developer RMZ Corp is seeking to raise about $500 million from Bain Capital to fund its property expansion across India.
stories.why: Following how major private equity firms structure deals in growth markets provides insight into private capital deployment and real estate investing.

stories.headline: AI Systems Disprove Decades-Old Computer Science Theory
stories.body: AI models built by Anthropic and OpenAI disproved a theoretical computer science concept that researchers studied for decades. Computer scientist Peter Jonsson said much of his upcoming conference presentation was rendered obsolete after the AI solved the problem in two days.
stories.why: As AI handles complex theoretical research, future software startups will focus more on practical application rather than manual algorithm design.

stories.headline: Google Releases Gemini 4 Carbon for Software Security
stories.body: Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon, a new AI model focused on identifying and fixing vulnerabilities in code. The model costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, outperforming competing models in benchmark tests.
stories.why: Automated code auditing is rapidly becoming a standard enterprise feature, lowering development costs for technical founders.

stories.headline: BCG Projects AI Could Cut $200 Billion from IT Services Work by 2030
stories.body: A report by Boston Consulting Group estimates that AI automation could reduce traditional IT services spending by $200 billion by 2030. BCG notes that IT firms will need to shift from charging by employee hours to pricing based on business outcomes.
stories.why: Consultants will be needed to help enterprise clients restructure vendor contracts and transition workforce structures as AI automates routine tasks.

stories.headline: UCI Museum Opens Exhibition on Artist Tokio Ueyama
stories.body: The UC Irvine Langson Orange County Museum of Art opened an exhibition titled Tokio Ueyama: The Hollows Between Mountains, featuring landscape, still life, and portrait work that captures Japanese immigrant communities.

stories.headline: Elena Rybakina Clinches Her First Year-End World No. 1 Ranking
stories.body: Elena Rybakina secured the year-end World No. 1 ranking for the first time in her career after defeating Yulia Putintseva in the second round of the Toray Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo.

term.name: Outcome-Based Pricing
term.definition: Outcome-based pricing is a model where a customer pays based on the specific results or financial returns delivered, rather than paying for employee hours or headcount. In today's news, BCG reports that AI automation is forcing tech and consulting services to abandon hourly billing in favor of outcome-based pricing.

serve.headline: Simplismart Raises $14M for AI Infrastructure
serve.body: Bengaluru startup Simplismart raised $14 million in a Series B round led by Dallas Venture Capital, with participation from Nvidia and Accel. The company builds software to help businesses run AI models more efficiently.
